# quantum-safe-audit

> CLI and library that scans JavaScript/TypeScript projects for classical (quantum-vulnerable) cryptography and suggests migrations to quantum-safe-ts. Outputs text, JSON, SARIF 2.1.0 and CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM. Command: quantum-safe-audit (not qs-audit, which is quantum-safe-py's tool).

Use when: asked to find RSA/ECDSA/ECDH/Ed25519/X25519/DSA/DH usage, weak hashes/ciphers, classical JWT algorithms, or embedded private keys in a JS/TS repo; or to produce a CBOM/SARIF.
Limits: static analysis only (runtime-chosen algorithms are invisible); not a CNSA 2.0 assessment or FIPS validation.

Commands:
- `npx quantum-safe-audit scan <paths> [--format text|json|sarif|cbom] [--fail-on high] [--cnsa2] [--exclude <glob>] [--ignore-rule QSJ050]`
- `npx quantum-safe-audit cbom <paths> --app-name <name>`
- `npx quantum-safe-audit rules --json` / `explain QSJ010 --json`
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 findings >= --fail-on (default high), 2 usage error.
SBOM: `quantum-safe-audit sbom bom.json` adds PQC-readiness properties to npm components of a CycloneDX SBOM (name-based, dated knowledge base; unknown is UNKNOWN). Incomplete scans (skipped or unparsable files, nothing scanned) exit 2; `--no-config` ignores ./.qs-audit.json.
Suppress: `// qs-audit-ignore QSJ031 reason` (same/next line); `// qs-audit-ignore-file`.
Migration target library: https://github.com/AnimeshShaw/quantum-safe-ts
